outcome: No change to the known bounds for the exact 2D axis-parallel-squares case (F(Q²)) has been found since 26 January 2024; recent activity in this area addresses higher-dimensional generalizations (cubes, balls) rather than the planar square case stated in this bullet.
summary: The covering problem of Rado (as stated in the bullet: axis-parallel squares of total unit area, largest guaranteed area of a disjoint sub-collection) has the long-standing known bounds of a greedy lower bound of 1/9 (Radó, 1928), and Ajtai's 1973 disproof of Radó's 1/4 conjecture giving an upper bound of 1/4 − 1/1728 ≈ 0.2494, later refined by Bereg, Dumitrescu and Jiang (2008/2009, published in Algorithmica) to an upper bound of 1/4 − 1/384 ≈ 0.2474 and a lower bound of roughly 1/8.4797 ≈ 0.1179. All of these predate the frozen revision by well over a decade, so they are background, not events in the window. Searches for work since 26 January 2024 turned up two relevant recent preprints: a semi-survey 'Rado's covering problem for cubes and balls' (arXiv 2604.17509, 2026-04) and 'On the weighted hard-core model and Rado's covering problem for congruent Euclidean balls' (arXiv 2608.09744, 2026-08). I fetched both directly (not just abstracts). Both explicitly restrict their new contributions to higher-dimensional cubes and to Euclidean balls (of any dimension, including the plane disk case for the second paper) and general symmetric convex bodies — neither reports any new bound for F(Q²), the exact axis-parallel-square case in the plane that this bullet asks about. Both merely restate the classical 1/9, Ajtai's 1/4−1/1728, and the 1/4−1/384 / ~1/8.4797 bounds as historical context. Under §3.1, a result about squares/balls in dimension d>2, or about disks/general convex bodies in the plane, is a related problem (a changed hypothesis class), not a case of the stated square problem, so even if either paper had produced a new bound for balls or cubes it would not count as a change to this bullet. I also checked two false leads from search noise: 'Symbolic Sets for Proving Bounds on Rado Numbers' (arXiv 2505.12085) concerns Rado numbers in Ramsey theory (monochromatic solutions to linear equations under colorings), an entirely different Rado problem sharing only the name; and 'Covering a square by congruent squares' (arXiv 2601.16535) is the unrelated problem of covering one square by smaller congruent squares (Erdős–Soifer-type problem), not Rado's disjoint-subset-area covering problem. No AI system appears anywhere in either genuinely relevant paper (2604.17509, 2608.09744): both rely purely on classical combinatorial/geometric/probabilistic arguments (hard-core lattice gas models, Brunn–Minkowski, sphere-packing bounds). I found no arXiv preprint, lab announcement, or Wikipedia lead change indicating any AI involvement with this problem in any form. The Wikipedia article's own current content (fetched directly) still reports only the pre-2024 bounds. I am satisfied nothing has happened to the exact stated problem in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue that since Rado's covering problem is usually stated as a general family F(K) over convex bodies K, the 2026 papers on cubes/balls/general symmetric convex bodies are progress 'on the covering problem of Rado' in a broad sense. But the Wikipedia bullet specifically restricts to axis-parallel squares with unit area in the plane, which is the F(Q²) case; per §3.1 this is the stated question, and generalizing to other bodies or higher dimensions changes rather than restricts it, so it is a related problem, not a case.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or publication that specifically narrows the gap between 1/8.4797 and 1/4−1/384 for the planar axis-parallel-square case F(Q²), or that settles the exact value of F(Q²).
